subject: Request: carveout for carrier transit incidents impacting private VPC latency
messages:
From: NebulaGrid Ops <ops@nebulagrid.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Oct 2028 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: persistent tail-latency spikes during ISP maintenance windows

Hi Naomi / team,

We’re seeing recurring 150–400ms tail-latency spikes for requests served from our private VPC that correspond exactly with nightly maintenance windows from our transit ISP (see attached packet traces). These are short (3–8 minutes) but frequent, and they’re causing automated health checks and downstream orchestrators to trigger failovers.

We need two things from Redwood:
- An operational acknowledgement that carrier/transit instability is considered a customer-managed dependency for private deployments, and an explicit carveout in the SLA for these events.
- A clear runbook for how Redwood will triage and mitigate (e.g., temporary routing to dedicated pool or short-term fallback to hosted model) when they occur.

We’d like to formalize a carveout for transit/carrier-caused latency incidents (with evidence-based attribution). Can you advise next steps and proposed wording?

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Infra Lead, NebulaGrid
ops@nebulagrid.com

Attachments: nebulagrid-pkt-trace-20281003.txt (packet trace), neb-config-snippets.txt (router config excerpt)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <infra-lead@nebulagrid.com>, NebulaGrid Ops <ops@nebulagrid.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Oct 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: persistent tail-latency spikes during ISP maintenance windows

Carlos — thanks for the traces and the clear symptom description. I’ve pulled the packet captures into our diagnostics and we can reproduce the amplification during the windows you call out.

High-level proposal from Redwood:
- We accept carrier/transit instability as a customer-controlled dependency for Private/VPC deployments and are willing to add a narrow SLA carveout for these incidents when evidence supports attribution to customer network/transit.
- Carveout conditions: packet/flow traces + BGP session/log evidence or ISP maintenance notification; event duration < 1h unless repeated within a 24h window.
- Operational mitigations: Redwood can offer a temporary routing fallback to our Dedicated pool for up to 6 hours subject to capacity and credits; or auto-throttled retry behavior to avoid cascade failovers.

I’ll draft proposed legal-friendly wording and loop Legal & Platform to confirm the telemetry/evidence requirements. Attaching a first-pass draft of the carveout and the trace we used for analysis.

Next step: internal alignment (I’ll ping Marcus and KP for the legal/ops wording). If this looks directionally right to you, we’ll circulate a formal addendum.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
aomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed-carveout-draft-v1.docx, nebulagrid-pkt-trace-20281003.txt

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: persistent tail-latency spikes during ISP maintenance windows

Marcus / KP — forwarding the ask from NebulaGrid. Key asks: carveout language for carrier/transit instability, evidence checklist (packet trace + ISP notice/BGP), and a short mitigation offer (temporary Dedicated routing or retry throttling).

Questions for legal/ops:
- Marcus: are the evidence requirements above defensible for SLA language? Any changes to duration/aggregation?
- KP: can Platform commit to a 6-hour temporary routing fallback subject to capacity? If not, what’s realistic (1–2 hours)?

I’d like to keep the carveout narrow so it’s not a blanket SLA escape — specific attribution and short-duration exception.

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: persistent tail-latency spikes during ISP maintenance windows

Naomi / KP — quick thoughts from Legal:
- Wording should emphasize evidence-driven attribution and mutual cooperation for collection (NebulaGrid must provide packet captures and ISP maintenance notices).
- Recommend limiting automatic credit triggers: carveout removes credit entitlement for incidents that are fully attributed to customer-managed transit; however, Redwood will provide a goodwill operational credit for repeated incidents at our discretion if we cannot reasonably reroute.
- Suggest tightening the time aggregation: carveout applies to single events up to 60 minutes; repeated events within a 24h span will be evaluated and may not be automatically carved out.

I’m okay with the proposed mitigation offer as an operational, non-contractual commitment ("Operational Mitigation Program") that can be exercised subject to capacity and with documented runbook steps. If NebulaGrid wants a firm capacity-backed SLA, that’s a different contract add-on.

Marcus
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <infra-lead@nebulagrid.com>, NebulaGrid Ops <ops@nebulagrid.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Oct 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed Private VPC transit-carveout (draft) — NebulaGrid review

Carlos — please find below the draft carveout language and operational notes. I’ve included the evidence checklist and the mitigation program terms.

DRAFT (proposed contract addendum excerpt):
"Carrier/transit dependency carveout: For Private/VPC deployments where the Customer manages ingress/egress transit, Redwood shall not be liable for SLA credits for incidents where (a) Customer demonstrates by packet/flow traces and ISP maintenance notice or BGP session logs that the root cause resides in Customer-managed transit or upstream carrier; and (b) the incident duration for any single attribution window is 60 minutes or less. Repeated attribution windows within a rolling 24-hour period are subject to joint review and may, at Redwood’s sole discretion, be excluded from the carveout if evidence indicates compound service degradation or misconfiguration on Customer infrastructure."

Operational Mitigation Program (non-contractual): Upon validated attribution to Customer-managed transit, Redwood will, subject to available capacity and with reasonable prior notice when practicable, offer temporary routing to Redwood Dedicated capacity for up to 6 hours per incident or enable auto-retry throttling to reduce cascade failovers. Any utilization of Dedicated capacity under this program will be billed at the customer’s committed rates or covered by a mutually agreed credit where applicable.

Evidence checklist: packet/flow trace (PCAP or equivalent), router/switch maintenance notice from ISP, BGP session logs, and a short annotated timeline prepared by Customer.

Please review and tell us any changes you’d like. If acceptable, we’ll push a formal addendum through DocuSign and include a short runbook for the mitigation steps.

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachments: proposed-carveout-draft-v1.docx

From: Carlos Mendez <infra-lead@nebulagrid.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: NebulaGrid Ops <ops@nebulagrid.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed Private VPC transit-carveout (draft) — NebulaGrid review

Naomi — thank you, this looks reasonable and appropriately narrow. We accept the carveout language as written, and NebulaGrid will commit to the evidence checklist for future incidents. We also appreciate the Operational Mitigation Program offer; we may request Dedicated routing on a case-by-case basis and will follow the runbook once you circulate it.

Please route the DocuSign addendum and we’ll get this signed.

— Carlos
